terms.meaning: Two angles side by side on a straight line, formed where two lines cross.
The angles opposite each other where two lines cross.
Lines on the same flat surface that never meet.
A line that crosses two or more lines at different points.

items.name: Angles in a linear pair
items.example: If one is 110°, the other is 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.name: Rule for vertically opposite angles
items.example: If one angle is 110°, the opposite one is 110°, and the other two are 70°.

items.name: Angles made by a transversal
items.formula: Two lines and a transversal make 8 angles

items.name: Corresponding angles
items.formula: Equal when the lines are parallel
items.example: If one is 135°, the corresponding angle is 135°.

items.name: Alternate angles
items.formula: Equal when the lines are parallel
items.example: If one is 60°, the alternate angle is 60°.

items.name: Inner angles on the same side
items.formula: Add up to 180° when the lines are parallel
items.example: If one is 60°, the other is 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.name: Testing for parallel lines
items.formula: Equal corresponding angles mean the lines are parallel
items.example: If corresponding angles are 75° and 80°, the lines are not parallel.

mistakes.text: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal only when the lines are parallel. Check that first.
Do not mix these up: a linear pair adds up to 180°, while vertically opposite angles are equal.
Lines that do not meet on the page may still meet if extended. Parallel lines never meet, however far they go.
